section: Accidental Deaths and Suicides in India 1995
title: ACCIDENTAL DEATHS & SUICIDES IN INDIA - 1995 N.C.R.B.(M.H.A.) 2.7.6 The table below represents the percentage share of each means of suicide during 1994 & 1995. It is observed from the table that in 12.5% cases the means of suicides could not be specified in 1994 whereas after revision in the input proforma the percentage of unspecified means came down to 7.17%. It is also observed that 'Poison' and 'Hanging' which are most prominent means showed marginal increases in incidence rising to 37.5% from 34.8% and 24.4% from 23.4% respectively over 1994. Data on 'over alcoholism', collected this year showed only 1.06% of total suicidal deaths due to this cause. It can be seen from the table that there were increases in 1995 over 1994 in all cases except for the means 'by fire/self immolation', 'by touching electric wire' and by 'coming under running vehicle/train' where a slight decline in incidence was noticed. Suicides by 'Fire-arms' remained more or less constant in terms of percentage share in All India in both the years.
